slides.headline: Metronomics Kick Off
notes: A 2-day workshop for the CEO and leadership team. Establish functional ownership and shared direction before annual and quarterly commitments. This reusable deck needs no company-specific edits.

slides.title: Byron Darlison
slides.headline: Byron Darlison
body: I built and sold a technology company after scaling it with the Metronomics operating system.
Now I coach founders to do in 3 years what took me 33.
notes: Scroll the timeline on the right. The moment in focus grows its photo or logo.
Leave it alone for 5 seconds and it tours itself, one moment every 3.5 seconds.

slides.title: I tried to scale five times. Only one worked.
slides.headline: I tried to scale five times.

figure.alt: Cash from 1989 to 2022. It stays flat with small bumps through four attempts to scale. After the fifth, in 2018, it climbs steeply. It ends at a 270 times return on coaching

attempts.heading: Raised venture capital
attempts.support: I thought money was the problem.

attempts.heading: Sold 49% to a bigger company
attempts.support: I thought they would know how.

attempts.heading: Hired a president
attempts.support: I thought someone else could do it better.

attempts.heading: Tried to self-implement Scaling Up
attempts.support: I thought I could do it on my own.

notes: Four tries on my own fell short. The fifth added a coach, a system and one customer.

1996: more money, same founder doing everything. 2001: an LED sign maker took a stake, same problem, no system. 2004: a new leader with no system to run. 2017: Scaling Up and Topgrading without a coach. 2018: one customer, K-12 schools in North America, and a year of cash in the bank by 2020.
Every try without a system made a bump, then fell back. The line only turned when we installed the system and picked one customer.

270x: the increase in enterprise value from 2018 to the sale, divided by everything I paid my coach. It includes the two and a half years after the formal engagement ended, while the system kept running.

slides.title: Share professional good news.
slides.headline: Share professional good news.
notes: Ask everyone for one piece of good news. Keep each contribution to 5 to 10 seconds. Coach models the pace.
At the Kick Off, use professional good news on Day 1 and personal good news on Day 2. At a quarterly, use professional good news.
Build positive connection and recognize progress. Explain the purpose before the round.

artwork.alt: Simple gray figures share positive news around a table.

slides.title: Introduce yourself.
slides.headline: Introduce yourself.
notes: Go around the team. Surface different interpretations without trying to solve the Function Chart yet.

panels.heading: Time here
panels.support: How long have you been with the company?

panels.heading: Accountability
panels.support: What is the #1 thing you are accountable for?

panels.heading: Success
panels.support: How do you measure success in your role numerically?

slides.title: Tell me about yourself.
slides.headline: Tell me about yourself.
notes: Coach shares first, then CEO, then the team. Invite people to share only what they are comfortable sharing. Allow room for listening.

panels.heading: Family
panels.support: What number child are you, out of how many?

panels.heading: A memory
panels.support: Describe a memorable event from before age 12.

slides.title: Today, let’s:
slides.headline: Today, let’s:
notes: Confirm agreement on how the team will work. Invite difficult facts and constructive disagreement.
Strong convictions, loosely held: argue your view fully, and change it when the facts change.
Disagree and commit: say where you disagree while everyone is in the room. Once the team decides, everyone backs the decision outside it.

panels.heading: No blame. No shame.
panels.support: Make it safe to speak honestly.

panels.heading: Disagree and commit
panels.support: Say it in the room, then back the decision.

slides.title: What did the prep survey tell us?
slides.headline: What did the prep survey tell us?

panels.heading: Where you differ
panels.support: Hear each view. Decide later in the agenda.

notes: Hand back the compiled survey answers now, printed or on the board. Go question by question, with everyone’s words side by side. Do not assume everyone has read them.

Do not read the answers aloud. Pick the 2 or 3 questions where the answers differ most. Ask each author what they meant, without debate. Park each difference on the board beside the agenda block that will resolve it. Use the Function Chart, the KFFM, purpose or the targets.
Allow about 15 minutes. Today is for decisions, not data gathering.

slides.title: What would make these 2 days valuable?
slides.headline: What would make these 2 days valuable?
notes: Ask each person to write an answer on a sticky note and share it. Agree on the answers. Return to these at the close. Allow 10 minutes.
The coach’s own answer is “Team clarity and commitment”. Hold it back until everyone has shared theirs, so it does not lead the room. It shows on the “Did we get what we came for?” slide.
slides.support: Write your answer, then share it with the team.

artwork.alt: A blank sticky note with a large question mark on it.

slides.title: Agree on the direction. Then commit to the work.
slides.headline: Agree on the direction. Then commit to the work.
notes: This is a working session. Protect time for the team to make decisions and capture its own plan.
Metronomics grows the team and the plan together: a shared playbook, a visible scoreboard and an outside coach.
